key_findings: Complete Roman city preserved under tephra. ~20000 inhabitants. Most famous volcanic burial site worldwide.
notes: Benchmark site. 6 m average: 2.5 m tephra fall + 3.5 m pyroclastic surge.

key_findings: Smaller city buried much deeper than Pompeii by pyroclastic flows. Preserved organic materials including wood and food.
reference: Sigurdsson et al. 1985 AJS; Mastrolorenzo et al. 2001 Nature
notes: 20-25 m depth — only partially excavated. Demonstrates extreme burial depths possible.

key_findings: Roman villa with frescoes. Same eruption as Pompeii.
notes: Similar depth to Pompeii.

key_findings: Minoan settlement preserved under massive tephra deposit. Multi-story buildings. Often called 'Minoan Pompeii'.
notes: Up to 30+ m of tephra. Only ~3% excavated.

key_findings: Maya village preserved under 5 m of tephra. 'Pompeii of the Americas'. Preserved garden beds and daily life.
notes: UNESCO World Heritage. Unique preservation of commoner settlement. 14 structures excavated.

key_findings: Modern town destroyed by lahar. 23000 dead. Buried under 3+ m of lahars.
notes: Modern disaster. Shows lahar burial can destroy and bury settlements instantly.

key_findings: Village buried by pyroclastic flow. ~200 dead. 1-3 m deposits.
reference: Pardini et al. 2019 Nat Hazards Earth Syst Sci
notes: Modern analogue for ancient volcanic burial events.

key_findings: Hindu temple (9th century) buried 6.5 m under Merapi volcanic deposits. Primary VOLCARCH calibration site.
notes: Discovered by accident. Excavated by Balai Arkeologi. Shows cumulative burial over ~1000 years.

key_findings: Hindu temple buried ~4 m under Merapi lahar deposits. Incomplete excavation.
notes: Discovered during sand mining. Only partially excavated. Demonstrates ongoing burial.

key_findings: Mataram Kuno settlement (8th-10th century) buried by Sindoro eruption. Houses foundations and artifacts.
notes: Most important buried settlement in Java. Multiple eruption layers. Ongoing excavation.

key_findings: Small Hindu temple complex buried under Merapi deposits. Discovered during UII campus construction.
notes: Recent discovery. Shallow burial compared to Sambisari.

key_findings: Silver Vishnu statue found at 9.14 m depth during well construction near Prambanan. Deepest documented find.
notes: Deepest documented archaeological find in Java's volcanic zone. Evidence for extreme burial.

key_findings: Capital of Majapahit Empire. Structures buried 1-3 m under volcanic deposits from Arjuno-Welirang system.
reference: Pojoh 2007 BIPPA; Satari 1977 Berita Penelitian Arkeologi
notes: Multiple excavation campaigns. GPR survey by Pojoh 2007. Ongoing urban development threatens site.

key_findings: Hindu temples (7th-8th century) partially buried by volcanic deposits on active Dieng Plateau.
notes: Temples cleared in colonial period. Ongoing volcanic activity continues to deposit material.

key_findings: Largest Hindu temple complex in East Java. Survived 1919 Kelud lahar but received tephra fall. Not deeply buried but lahar came within 2 km.
notes: Near-miss control case. Shows stochastic nature of volcanic destruction.

key_findings: Monument partially buried by vegetation and volcanic debris over centuries. Major restoration 1907-1911 and 1975.
notes: Not fully buried due to enormous size, but lower galleries were buried 1+ m.

key_findings: Settlement of Tambora kingdom destroyed by 1815 eruption. Called 'Pompeii of the East'. Carbonized remains.
notes: Discovered by Sigurdsson expedition. Buried under 3+ m of pyroclastic deposits.

key_findings: Homo erectus child skull. Volcanic matrix. Found in Pleistocene volcanic deposits.
notes: Different time scale (Pleistocene) but same volcanic burial mechanism.

key_findings: Middle Paleolithic tools found above and below Toba tephra layer ~15 cm thick. 2000+ km from source.
notes: Distal Toba impact. Archaeological continuity debated. Shows tephra fall at extreme distance.

key_findings: Modern city abandoned and buried by ongoing eruption. 2/3 of island evacuated.
reference: Wadge et al. 2014 Geol Soc London Mem
notes: Modern analogue. City progressively buried over 2+ years.

key_findings: Modern town partially buried by 1994 eruption tephra. Town abandoned and relocated.
notes: Modern analogue. Shows rapid burial of urban area.

key_findings: Modern town partially destroyed and buried by lahars and tephra during 2008 eruption.
notes: Modern analogue. Lahar burial dominated.

key_findings: Bronze Age village preserved under Avellino eruption tephra. Hut impressions and footprints.
notes: Older than Pompeii. Same volcano. Shows repeated burial cycle.

key_findings: Roman villa with treasure. Same eruption as Pompeii.
notes: Slightly shallower than Pompeii center.

key_findings: Roman resort town. Pliny the Elder died here.
notes: Same eruption sequence as Pompeii.

key_findings: Pre-Aztec ceremonial center buried under 8 m of Xitle lava. Lava burial differs from tephra — preserves shape but destroys organics.
notes: Lava burial — different preservation mechanism from tephra. Circular pyramid.

key_findings: Neolithic settlement. Volcanic imagery in murals. Thin tephra layer identified in stratigraphy but not buried by eruption.
notes: Debated volcanic connection. Thin tephra fall — not burial event.

key_findings: Pre-Columbian settlement buried by Laguna Caldera eruption. Contemporary with Cerén.
notes: Less famous than Cerén but same time period.

key_findings: Multiple settlements buried by Tierra Blanca Joven tephra from Ilopango caldera.
notes: Major regional impact. Depopulated western El Salvador for decades.
